newsitem.title: USA: Plains feedlot cattle market inactive - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains feedlot cattle market inactive - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains cattle markets were quiet Wednesday, with packers and cattle sellers locked in a stalemate, feedlot sources said.
Packers bid $70.00 per cwt against firm asking levels of $72.00, with neither side budging, the sources said.
Market watchers said they expect trading to take place Thursday at least unchanged from last week's top price of $72.00 to possibly $73.00.
Prices were seen supported by ideas packers were getting short on live inventories, the feedlot sources said.

Feedlot cattle prices also were expected to be bolstered by tight supplies of market-ready cattle on showlists despite a modest carryover from last week because a number of cattle remained 'green' or underfinished, the sources said.
Support in cattle prices could be offset, however, by a drop in boxed beef prices, they said.
Boxed beef prices at midday were quoted down $0.35 to $0.51 per cwt, with 203 fabricated loads sold, according to USDA.
